Title: ReactiveCircus/android-emulator-runner
Summary: Most-used CI Action for headless emulators; community-consensus config. Default flags are load-bearing and very likely worth mirroring locally: -no-window -gpu swiftshader_indirect -no-snapshot -noaudio -no-boot-anim. Documents AVD snapshot caching (cache ~/.android/avd/* + ~/.android/adb*; first run makes a clean snapshot, later runs use -no-snapshot-save) as the biggest startup win, plus disable-animations, API 29+, x86_64, default/google_apis targets, emulator-boot-timeout (600s). Its swiftshader_indirect default independently corroborates the project's finding that host GPU can't render RN Fabric here. Read entrypoint scripts for the exact boot-poll loop. [found by 2 agents]

Title: Android Debug Bridge (adb) | Android Developers
Summary: Authoritative Google reference and the canonical citation for the core readiness pitfall: adb devices reports state=device while the OS is still booting, so connection state does NOT imply readiness. States: offline / device (connected, not necessarily booted) / no device. Confirms `adb shell getprop sys.boot_completed` == 1 only when fully booted. Documents screencap capture (`adb exec-out screencap -p > screen.png`). wait-for-device / get-state are standard subcommands. Almost certainly the first reference for any boot-readiness design — directly relevant to the stale-emulator-state confusion.

Title: Maestro Best Practices: Structuring your Test Suite
Summary: Maestro-owned, authoritative. Core principle: a Flow tests ONE user scenario, not a monolith — better parallelism, debuggability, isolation. Feature-grouped subdirs (auth/, checkout/, common/) plus a config.yaml flows: glob block (only root-level flows run by default). Tag-based selective execution (--include-tags smokeTest) for PR-vs-nightly. Very likely the best starting reference for suite layout; pair with nested-flows + Android docs for syntax and platform specifics.

Title: How to Avoid Flaky Tests with Built-In Tolerance
Summary: Maestro-owned; the most relevant page to the project's 'post-action settle' cost. Documents tolerance internals very likely worth tuning: ~17s element-lookup timeout, 2s animation-settle (10x200ms), 0.5% screenshot-diff stability threshold for animation-end, 7s optional-element window. Real devices add 50-200ms touch latency vs emulators. Strongly warns against sleep() (up to 16min wasted across 50 tests) and reserves extendedWaitUntil for rare long waits. disableAnimations: true in config.yaml cuts cross-platform animation flakiness; identical YAML across Views/Compose/RN. Title: Maestro Docs — driver startup timeout
Summary: Authoritative. Confirms env var MAESTRO_DRIVER_STARTUP_TIMEOUT (milliseconds). Platform defaults: Android 15000ms, iOS 120000ms. Doc bumps to 180000ms for slow/CI hosts. Very likely the single most useful lever for 'Android driver did not start up in time' on a loaded laptop, and almost certainly applies to the Bubble CLI runs (driver pins host port 7001). Answers the readiness-timeout area; pair with an emulator boot-complete wait BEFORE invoking Maestro.

Title: Five strategies to address Android emulator instability during automated testing | QA Wolf
Summary: Testing-company article, directly on resilience. (1) Disable noise features (GPS, cameras, sensors, hw.gps=no, -no-skin). (2) Pin resources per instance (Docker --cpus=2 --memory=4g, isolated disk; avoid shared runners). (3) Control environment (wired net, freeze versions, disable auto-update). (4) Pre-booted/warm snapshots cut startup minutes->seconds and bypass the flaky first boot that spikes CPU 80-100%. (5) System-level resilience via structured logging + failure-signature analysis over blind retries. Frames instability as resource/timing exposure. Snapshot advice partly conflicts with cold-boot-for-stability sources — the right tradeoff about as likely as not depends on snapshot-corruption rate. [found by 2 agents]

Title: Troubleshoot known issues with Android Emulator | Android Developers
Summary: Google-authoritative. CI-relevant fixes: keep 5+GB free disk; force cold boot with -no-snapshot (or -no-snapshot-load); reset with -wipe-data; disable Vulkan via `-feature -Vulkan` for render glitches/snapshot-creation failures (esp. Apple Silicon MoltenVK, Chrome API30+); -gpu swiftshader for GPU-compat issues; -dns-server 8.8.8.8 for no-internet. Multi-emulator gotchas: duplicate MAC -> only first instance gets internet. Whitelist emulator in antivirus to avoid snapshot I/O degradation. Explicit CI takeaway: -no-snapshot -wipe-data for clean reproducible runs. Very likely the canonical fallback for any boot/hang/render failure.

Title: awesome-android-scripts/wait-for-device.sh
Summary: Concrete, copyable readiness script: `adb wait-for-device` then `while [[ -z $(getprop sys.boot_completed) ]]; do sleep 1; done`, then wakes the screen / presses HOME. Cautionary detail directly relevant to robustness: NO timeout, so it can hang forever if boot never completes. Very likely a good base pattern, but add an iteration cap and probably a bootanim or input-dispatcher check on top.

Title: Checklist for Reducing Test Flakiness
Summary: Maestro-owned resilience checklist. (1) Dynamic/condition waits over fixed sleeps. (2) Stable locators — testIDs/roles/visible text, avoid absolute XPath/position/dynamic IDs, centralize in a page object. (3) Independent self-contained tests, unique IDs (UUID/timestamp), mocked externals, idempotent. (4) Stable env — containers/pinned versions, reset state per run, monitor CPU/RAM. (5) Auto-retry ~2x, mark retry-passes flaky, @flaky -> nightly quarantine, investigate <95% pass. (6) Monitoring + retained traces/video. Somewhat web-flavored (data-testid/CSS); waits/locators/quarantine guidance translates directly to Maestro YAML.

Title: How to run an Android emulator on GitHub Actions
Summary: Practitioner walkthrough, copy-pasteable. KVM udev rule. Launch flags: -no-window -gpu swiftshader_indirect -noaudio -no-boot-anim -memory 8192 -cores 4 -no-snapshot-load -no-snapshot-save (cold boot to avoid RAM-snapshot corruption). Advanced pre-baked state via QCOW2 overlay + base disk (relative backing paths via qemu-img rebase -u); back up overlays since they sometimes get corrupted. Notes swiftshader_indirect works headless while swangle may be needed locally for some logins. Likely directly useful for the baked-logged-in-AVD idea in the e2e backlog; the QCOW2 overlay technique is the novel content.

Title: Detect when Android emulator is ready
Summary: Focused, practical. The alternative readiness signal: poll `adb shell getprop init.svc.bootanim` until it returns 'stopped'. Complements sys.boot_completed — bootanim=stopped is about as likely as not a slightly stronger 'UI settled' signal. Dated (2014) but the properties remain valid. Does not discuss the device-state-vs-boot pitfall, so pair with the adb docs.

Title: Maestro in GitHub Action times out 'Android driver did not start up in time' #965
Summary: Maestro-owned issue. Root cause: emulator not fully ready when Maestro connects in resource-constrained CI; a PR raised the default timeout to 15s, and this thread is where the configurable timeout was requested (now shipped as MAESTRO_DRIVER_STARTUP_TIMEOUT). Fix path = increase timeout + ensure emulator boot-complete first. The readiness-race story is about as likely as not the same one biting CLI runs on a loaded laptop.

Title: Test discovery and tags — Maestro Docs
Summary: Authoritative. Only top-level flows run unless config.yaml flows: globs include subdirs (auth/*, tests/**). Tags in flow headers; CLI --include-tags/--exclude-tags use OR within a flag and AND across flags; config.yaml includeTags/excludeTags set workspace policy, CLI takes precedence. Worked example shows exclude overriding include. Directly relevant to the smoke/ios/android tagging and platform-scoped runs.

Title: Configure hardware acceleration for the Android Emulator
Summary: Google-authoritative on GPU modes/hypervisors. Modes: auto (default), host (highest quality, MoltenVK on macOS), software/swiftshader/swangle/lavapipe. CI/headless: recommends software/swiftshader. Hypervisors: KVM (Linux), Hypervisor.Framework (macOS), WHPX (Windows). -accel-check/kvm-ok to verify.

Title: Parallel Testing on Android and iOS
Summary: Maestro-owned, speed-focused. Sharding: --shard-all N (full suite per device) vs --shard-split N (split across devices); e.g. maestro test --device 'emulator-5554,...' --shard-all 2 ./tests. Isolation: clearState: true, and ${MAESTRO_SHARD_INDEX}/${MAESTRO_DEVICE_UDID} in artifact filenames to avoid collisions (matches the project's sanitizeFileName/run-scoped rules). Warns macOS limits local iOS parallelism and iOS sims hit port conflicts (matches 'run platforms sequentially, use 2 sims'). Cites a 16h->under-1h result. Likely the best lead for cutting wall-clock once stability is in hand.

Title: How to execute Android UI tests on CI and stay alive | Wix Engineering
Summary: Experienced practitioner (Detox team). Prefer AOSP (Google-free) images for stability (parallels the project's ATD/google_apis finding); bump AVD config.ini heap 576MB / RAM 2048MB; pre-boot to idle then gracefully shut down to persist a quick-boot snapshot; install LinkedIn Test Butler to suppress ANR/system dialogs that block automation; enable on-screen touch indicators for video diagnosis. No adb readiness scripts, but strong on snapshot + image-choice + dialog-suppression.

Title: Android Emulator Black Screen & adb 'device offline': Troubleshooting Fixes
Summary: Targeted troubleshooting of the exact black-screen + device-offline failure mode. Causes: insufficient resources, corrupted AVD/snapshot, GPU/driver, hypervisor conflicts, ADB desync, port-5037 contention. Diagnostics: adb kill-server && adb start-server && adb devices; emulator -avd <name> -verbose; lsof -i :5037. Fixes: Cold Boot Now to clear corrupted state, Software-GLES renderer for weak GPUs, AVD RAM <=50% host. Likely relevant to torn-snapshot/black detection, though it cites generic software-GLES rather than swiftshader.
